newsitem.title: USA: Carrington says drug trial disappointing.
newsitem.headline: Carrington says drug trial disappointing.

text.p: Carrington Laboratories Inc said on Thursday that the first Phase III Pivotal trial of its proprietary drug compound Aliminase in the treatment of ulcerative colitis failed to support a therapeutic effect.
The company said it placed on hold a second Phase III Pivotal trial while data from the first trial is examined to determine whether a change in formulation or a change in dosage regimen is merited.

"Although we are not pleased with the results from the ulcerative colitis study, we have gained a great deal of knowledge about Aliminase," said David Shand, Carrington executive vice president-research and development.

"Very recent data obtained on Aliminase resulted in the development of a patentable process that separates out various biological activities which in some of our compounds have different, and sometimes opposite, effects," he said.
"Our theory is that in ulcerative colitis, the desirable anti-inflammatory action may have been opposed by other effects of a separate part of the product."
Shand continued, "We plan to develop the newly separated anti-inflammatory component."
The results of the ulcerative colitis trial will have no effect on continuing Phase I trials of the drug CarraVex in the treatment of cancer, the company said.
Also, the trial results will not impact the launch of its DiaB line of diabetic products in November or the scheduled roll-out of the new RadiaCare line, Carrington said.
The company also said it plans to launch CarraSmart Film late this year and five additional wound-care products during the first quarter 1997.
